subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent integrations get an explicit persistent session mode, or should /hooks/agent remain isolated-only with docs clarifying that stable sessionKey is routing metadata rather than transcript continuity?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested behavior is still missing, but the fix changes public hook API/config surface and lets authenticated hook callers intentionally re-enter durable transcript context.

options.title: Accept explicit persistent mode
options.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated defaults and gates persistent reuse through hook auth, allowed prefixes, and agent allowlists.

options.title: Keep hooks isolated-only
options.body: Reject the persistent-mode direction and update docs to say hook-agent sessionKey does not preserve transcript continuity.

options.title: Design broader session identity
options.body: Pause the linked PR and define a wider deterministic session identity model for trusted hooks before adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit persistent mode
recommendation.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated defaults and gates persistent reuse through hook auth, allowed prefixes, and agent allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter supplied the latest product-direction comment for this exact issue and is the best available owner for the API/security choice.
